zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'X is directly left/right of Y', enforce that the house numbers differ by exactly 1, with the correct direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue explicitly mentions 'directly left of' or 'directly right of' between two entities.
zebralogic.example: Assuming X and Y can be any distance apart, which would miss the required adjacency.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says 'X is somewhere to the left/right of Y', enforce a strict ordering (X < Y or X > Y).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses non‑adjacent left/right phrasing without specifying exact distance.
zebralogic.example: Treating 'X is somewhere left of Y' as a direct adjacency, over‑constraining the layout.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., 'the person who loves grilled cheese is the person's ...'), enforce that the two attributes belong to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly links two attributes as being the same entity.
zebralogic.example: Treating linked attributes as independent and placing them in different houses.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., 'Peter lives in the sixth house'), assign that attribute to that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue provides an absolute house number for an attribute.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring a fixed‑house clue and leaving the attribute free, leading to multiple possible placements.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, double quotes, and correct nesting.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of reasoning, just before emitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Leaving a trailing comma or mismatched brackets, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier can parse it correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When constructing the final answer for a zebra‑logic puzzle.
zebralogic.example: Appending extra commentary after the JSON, causing the parser to miss the solution.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B, B = C), propagate the links so all linked attributes are assigned to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When several clues link attributes indirectly through other attributes.
zebralogic.example: Only linking pairs directly and missing the transitive connection, resulting in inconsistent assignments.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between two entities, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions 'N houses between', 'one house between', or similar phrasing.
zebralogic.example: Using a difference of N instead of N + 1, placing the entities too close together.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that a particular attribute value is not in a specific house (e.g., 'X is not in house 3'), ensure that the attribute is assigned to a different house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue includes a negative house constraint.
zebralogic.example: Placing the attribute in the forbidden house, violating the clue.

zebralogic.title: UndirectedAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says two entities are 'next to each other' (or 'adjacent') without specifying direction, enforce that the absolute difference in their house numbers is exactly 1, without imposing left/right ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like 'X and Y are next to each other', 'are adjacent', or similar, and does not specify left/right.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting a 'next to each other' clue as directional, assuming X is left of Y, which can discard the valid arrangement where Y is left of X.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart' (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the phrase as a simple distance rather than accounting for the intervening houses.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue mentions 'N houses between', add 1 to N to compute the required absolute house-number difference.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate reasoning or commentary after the JSON, exceeding the expected format.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Emit all reasoning first, then output the JSON as the very last part of the response, with no trailing text.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates too much text, exceeding the allowed token budget for the response.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and ensure the final JSON is placed at the end; avoid unnecessary verbosity.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model overlooks 'not in house X' clues when assigning attributes.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Explicitly check all negative house constraints before finalizing assignments.
